title: CLI flag to decline pre-baseline reconstruction (the iterative loop needs the window cut)
description: Task-188 finding (2026-07-25): the iterative reconstruct -> commit -> re-seed loop cannot actually start from the new hash, because preBaselineReconstructionAllowed defaults to true and ONLY the viewer flips it (src/reconstruction_base_commit.ts:33 — "the CLI never touches it"). computeSkippedBaselineCutoff therefore returns undefined on every CLI run, so a later --base-commit does not prune the records before it: the re-seeded run measured 48s vs the control 49s and its ladder still started ~11 hours before its own seed instant. Add the CLI equivalent of the viewer's "No" to the pre-baseline question (e.g. --no-pre-baseline) so a re-seeded iteration reconstructs only forward from the seed, then re-measure the loop with it. Evidence: plans/166-per-file-target.md, section "Task 188 — the iterative reconstruct -> commit -> re-seed loop".

title: Mid-stream base-commit seed yields a non-monotonic ladder with a duplicated snapshot revision
description: Task-188 finding (2026-07-25): seeding --base-commit at a commit INSIDE the recorded window (step 4 of the iterative loop) corrupts the emitted ladder for common/scripts/plate/plate_cli.py. The gitBase: overwrite lands at index 10 stamped 2026-05-14T03:06:21Z, before an index-11 revision stamped 2026-05-13T21:45:19Z (non-monotonic), and snapshot 04b5333dde2392bd@v2 appears TWICE (indices 8 and 11) where the same-bound control run against the original baseline emits it once — 20 revisions vs the control 18, entirely accounted for by those two artifacts. Both the control and iteration-1 ladders are monotonic, so the trigger is the mid-window seed placement (see reconstruction_git_placement.ts / seedBaseCommitBeacon in reconstruction_base_commit.ts). Fix the ordering + dedupe, or refuse a mid-window baseline with a clear error. May be resolved by task 223 (dropping pre-seed records) — verify before assuming. Evidence: plans/166-per-file-target.md, section "Task 188 — the iterative reconstruct -> commit -> re-seed loop".
